key_insight: A high-throughput DFT/minima-hopping search identified 58 stable CuI-based ternary compounds with promising p-type transparent conductor behavior, including 20 intrinsically degenerate semiconductors.
engineering_relevance: The work expands the design space for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics by showing that chemically tunable Cu–I halides can deliver both wide gaps and mobile holes.
method: Minima hopping structure search across X–Cu–I composition space
Density functional theory screening for stability, optical transparency, and hole effective mass
Revisiting CMVB design rules using the discovered compound dataset
evidence_signal: From the abstract, 58 candidates passed the screening filters, 49 were previously unreported, and Cu2FI2 was highlighted with a 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m0 hole effective mass.
watch_item: These are computational predictions, so experimental synthesis, defect control, and carrier mobility verification remain necessary before device adoption.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
